title: profile-as-code — user profile contract (v1.11)
description: Contract source (D3) for a profile-data workspace. The core `load()` parses content/*.yaml, merges them into a single Profile and validates against THIS schema. Facts (dates, DOIs, URLs, ORCID) are language-independent and are the GEO anchor. Every text field is a langMap ({lang: value}) with EN required (D8, §11). Additive since v1 (semver minor): every earlier workspace still validates. v1.1: role as langMap (org stays invariant string), highlights as string[] per lang, publication.authors/url, root languages + education, identity.handle/timezone, patreon in checks; brand flavor (D15/§17) — `flavor`, org identity variant (orgName/logo/brandVoice/mission/tagline/established), socialHandles/newsletter/podcast/press/audiences blocks, brand platforms, handle checks. New in v1.2 (D16): platform set = Postiz parity + operator extras — 43 platforms, one shared enum for both flavors, single-source dedup guard (check.platform). New in v1.3 (D18): per-entry deploy ledger — `deployments` (ledgerKey → surface → deployedAt/contentHash/source), optional stable `id`s on row blocks (experience/projects/publications/education/press), `origin: template` provenance flag. New in v1.4 (D17): evidence registry — `credentials[]` (third-party attestations: certificate/title/award/patent) and `artifacts[]` (works/media: portfolio/gallery/showreel/dataset/document/code), pointer-first (§18); `evidenceItem` gains `credentialId`/`artifactId` cross-refs, `publications[]`/`press[]` gain `artifactRefs`. Naming discipline (§18.1): the registry is never called evidence — `projects[].evidence[]` stays claims-only. New in v1.5 (issue #71): `identity.email` — the contact email as a first-class fact (schema.org `email` on Person/Organization), NOT a link — `links[]` stays http(s)-only (mailto: rejected, D12); a mailto: row in links[] broke the template and every real workspace after v1.4's scheme boundary (issue #53). New in v1.6 (issue #103): `identity.links[].role` — the link ROLE (`identity` | `realization` | `aggregator`), a translation layer onto schema.org (`url` | `sameAs` | `mainEntityOfPage`); absent role = `realization`, so every pre-v1.6 workspace stays VALIDATING unchanged (the rendered output does change — see §15.4). The JSON-LD `@id` is derived from the `role: identity` link and is ABSENT when no link carries it (never invented). Entity assembly moves to a single home (core/src/structured-data.ts), consumed by geoCheck and every renderer — the §18.9 credentialLdEntries precedent. New in v1.7 (issue #130): `kofi` — Ko-fi creator page as operator extra #10 (44 platforms), creator-monetization family; paste platform, no API deploy (D9). New in v1.8 (issue #133): `buymeacoffee`, `liberapay`, `gumroad`, `payhip` — the creator monetization platforms family (D16), operator extras #11–#14 (48 platforms); the family is declared in SPEC and descriptions (docs-first), not as a hard schema field; all four are paste platforms, no API deploy (D9). New in v1.9 (issue #137): `hotmart` — the Hotmart digital-products storefront + memberships (Members Area / recurring billing) serving the Spanish/Portuguese-speaking markets, in the `creator-monetization` family as operator extra #15 (49 platforms); paste platform, no API deploy (D9) — no management API is documented for the profile body (developers.hotmart.com covers sales/products [?], fetched 2026-10-05). New in v1.10 (issue #288): the answer-engine surface — `identity.definition` (the canonical per-language definition: ≤160 chars per value, must contain the entity name — the length cap is schema-enforced, the name check is a geoCheck rule, #289) and root `faq[]` (3–20 citable Q&A pairs: `q` ≤90 per value and unique per workspace, `a` ≤320, optional `$defs/url` `source`; below 3 there is no surface, above 20 it is a page, not a profile). `structuredData()` exposes `description` + a separate `FAQPage` JSON-LD node, emitted only when the fields exist. The same minor completes the version label of the §19.5 certification additions (issue #132 — shipped in `d172dffc` under the v1.9 URI). New in v1.11 (issue #334): `identity.nationality` — the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 nationality code as a citable fact (uppercase, e.g. `VE`); schema.org `Person.nationality` → `Country` with `identifier` on the JSON-LD. Optional and additive: a workspace that omits it validates and scores as before (it is outside the structured-data `ready` gate and completeness ratio).

identity.description: Canonical identity. THE source of truth for URLs and names (GEO anchor).

flavor.description: v1.1 (additive): workspace flavor (D15). person (default, absent = person) or brand. Brand enables the org identity variant, the socialHandles/newsletter/podcast/press/audiences blocks and Organization GEO (§17).

socialHandles.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): the brand handle matrix — one row per platform with claim status. Seeded from the operator's brand-handles availability sweep (§17).

newsletter.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): the brand's newsletter surface (Substack/Ghost).

podcast.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): the brand's podcast (Spotify show/RSS).

press.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): media mentions of the brand (verifiable, dated).

audiences.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): brand audiences — reader profiles (not recruiters). Audience name → per-lang angle (same shape as positioning.audiences; brand-facing).

positioning.description: Value proposition: statement, per-audience angles, GEO intent.

bios.description: Curated bio per platform+lang+length. Generated by `pasco refine`, chosen by the user, stored here.

headlines.description: Headline per platform+lang (the 1-line under the name).

education.description: v1.1 (additive): formal education. v1 workspaces keep education inside experience[] with role = degree.

languages.description: v1.1 (additive): spoken languages. v1 workspaces document them as comments in skills.yaml.

publications.description: Peer-reviewed / citable output. DOI/ORCID resolvable → GEO citability.

keywords.description: SEO per platform + GEO associations/claims (cross-cutting layer, D7).

checks.description: User-level declarative checks; unioned with the platform skill's checks.yaml by `pasco check`.

active.description: Which bio/headline variant is LIVE per platform (D11: user picks, engine records).

deployments.description: v1.3 (D18, §19): per-entry deploy ledger — ledgerKey → surface → record. Keys are constrained above for JSON Schema consumers; the generated Zod drops propertyNames, so core re-checks key patterns, surface enums, duplicate ids and ambiguous composite keys post-Zod (D12 fail class). Only `pasco` mutates this block (same write rule as refine --choose, D14).

credentials.description: v1.4 (D17, §18): the proof layer — third-party attestations (certificates, titles, awards, patents). Pointer-first: the workspace declares pointers, the engine never owns binaries (D14). Naming discipline (§18.1): never called evidence.

artifacts.description: v1.4 (D17, §18): works/media items (portfolio, gallery, showreel, dataset, document, code), pointer-first via `locator`. Naming discipline (§18.1): never called evidence — canonical blocks keep their domains (publications/press are NOT registry kinds, they reference registry ids).

faq.description: v1.10 (issue #288): the citable answer surface — the questions THIS entity answers, as fact pairs (never generated copy, D11/D14). 3–20 entries: below 3 there is no surface; above 20 it is a page, not a profile. `structuredData()` projects it as a `FAQPage` node ONLY when present (never an empty FAQPage); the citability rules beyond JSON Schema are geoCheck v2 (#289).

lang.description: Supported languages. EN required (international recruiters), ES native, FR desirable (D8).

langMap.description: Text in one or more languages. EN is ALWAYS required — a schema rule enforced by `pasco validate` (§11). Key restriction via propertyNames (enum en/es/fr). Value typing via additionalProperties (issue #86, F3): every consumer assumes Record<string, string>, so non-string values (0, [], {}) are invalid at the boundary — the generated Zod already enforced this (gen-zod materializes the langMap shape); the JSON Schema now matches it (no engine change). Empty strings stay schema-valid BY DESIGN — they count as ABSENT at the text accessor (issue #84, option (a) ratified).

langMapList.description: v1.1 (additive): like langMap but values are string arrays (bullets). Used by experience.highlights to express list-shaped content per language.

url.description: http(s) ONLY (issue #53): the SSOT validates the scheme at the boundary so renderers emit any SSOT URL verbatim with zero per-emit filtering. `format: uri` alone admits non-http schemes (javascript:, data:, vbscript:) — the pattern is the assertion; format stays as annotation for schema-aware consumers. Case-sensitive per ECMA-262 regex (JSON Schema patterns carry no flags); an uppercase scheme fails loudly (D12 fail class), it is not a security hole.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Facts are language-independent (GEO anchor). Month/year precision allowed (YYYY-MM via YYYY-MM-01).

platform.description: Platform set (ONE source, dedup). v1: person surfaces. v1.1 (additive, brand §17): brand surfaces + the socialHandles matrix key space. v1.2 (additive, D16): Postiz parity + operator extras — 43 platforms; new slugs Postiz-aligned verbatim (linkedin-page, instagram-standalone, devto, gmb, warpcast, moltbook, mewe, tumblr); ghost is an operator extra Postiz lacks (docs.postiz.com llms.txt: 34 providers, fetched 2026-09-02). v1.7 (issue #130): kofi — Ko-fi creator page, operator extra #10, 44 total; creator-monetization family, paste flow (D9). v1.8 (issue #133): buymeacoffee, liberapay, gumroad, payhip — creator monetization platforms (D16 family), operator extras #11–#14, 48 total; paste flow (D9). v1.9 (issue #137): hotmart — Hotmart digital-products storefront + memberships (Members Area / recurring billing), operator extra #15, 49 total; creator-monetization family, paste flow (D9).

email.description: v1.5 (additive, issue #71): contact email of the person/brand (schema.org `email` on Person/Organization). A fact like name/location — NOT a link: renderers emit it as a mailto: href in the Links section and as the JSON-LD `email` property; `sameAs` stays page-URLs-only. Lives OUTSIDE identity.links[] by design — the ^https?:// rule of $defs/url (issue #53) stays strict on every URL field, so a mailto: row in links[] fails validation (D12). RFC-5322-adjacent (issue #71 review): local part lax (no whitespace/quotes), domain hostname-shaped (labels [A-Za-z0-9-], no empty/trailing/consecutive dots — unicode domains must use punycode).

definition.description: v1.10 (issue #288): the canonical definition of this identity per language — one sentence of the form 'X is a …'; maps to schema.org `description` on `Person`/`Organization`.

orgName.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): legal/registered org name when it differs from the display name (name = display, e.g. 'Topia Press').

logo.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): logo URL (schema.org Organization logo).

brandVoice.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): tone matrix seed — tone + values + avoid. Per-platform voice lives in the platform skill.

mission.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): the brand's mission (schema.org Organization description).

tagline.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): the one-line tagline (schema.org Organization slogan).

established.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): founding date (schema.org Organization foundingDate).

nationality.description: v1.11 (issue #334): ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 nationality code (uppercase, e.g. `VE`), a fact distinct from `location` (residence). Maps to schema.org `Person.nationality` as a `Country` node with `identifier` on the JSON-LD. Person-only by the standard's model: a `flavor: brand` workspace may declare it (identity is shared) but the Organization branch emits no `nationality` node — the value is not silently rewritten into a brand fact. The pattern asserts ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 FORM only — `ve`, `Venezuela` and `VEN` fail loudly (ECMA-262 pattern, no flags; D12 fail class); membership in the published code list is not enforced. Optional: outside the structured-data `ready` gate and completeness ratio, so absence changes nothing.

role.description: v1.6 (#103): the ROLE this link plays with respect to the entity — a translation layer of this engine onto schema.org, never standard vocabulary. `identity` → schema.org:url (the page IS the entity; strong authority; the one eligible for JSON-LD @id). `realization` (DEFAULT when absent) → schema.org:sameAs (the page indirectly indicates the entity; weak authority; these — and only these — form the sameAs set). `aggregator` → schema.org:mainEntityOfPage (link-in-bio / redirector that aggregates references to the entity; medium authority; never eligible for @id). Absence keeps every pre-v1.6 workspace VALIDATING unchanged (additive, dev-methodology §3) — it does NOT keep the output byte-identical: v1.6 also makes github-readme emit jobTitle/worksFor, narrows sameAs to realization links (+ claimed handles), and adds the geo/entity-id gap report.

links.description: Canonical link set. Renderers and skills read URLs ONLY from here — no per-platform URL duplication (drift source). v1.6 (#103): items carry an optional `role` distinguishing the entity's own page (schema.org:url) from pages that merely indicate it (schema.org:sameAs) or aggregate references to it (schema.org:mainEntityOfPage).

audiences.description: Audience name → per-lang angle (e.g. recruiter / client / academia).

semanticAssociations.description: 3-5 anchors an LLM should associate with the person (e.g. 'física', 'innovación educativa', 'soberanía de IA'). Seeded without stuffing (§8).

geoKeywords.description: Terms a generative engine should match this skill with (GEO layer, D7).

platformWeights.description: How much this skill matters per platform (0..1). Feeds renderer keyword placement.

role.description: v1: string. v1.1 (additive): langMap — bilingual role titles.

org.description: Proper noun — invariant across languages (e.g. 'USFQ', 'Nimbus Labs'). Not a langMap: institutions are never translated (SPEC §11).

highlights.description: v1: langMap of strings (separator-delimited). v1.1 (additive): langMap of string arrays (bullets).

experienceItem.description: start <= end is NOT expressible in JSON Schema — enforced by core.driftCheck (§12 note).

degree.description: v1.1: degree title (string or bilingual langMap).

institution.description: Proper noun — invariant across languages (e.g. 'Universidad Central de Venezuela'). Not a langMap: institutions are never translated (SPEC §11).

field.description: v1.1: field of study (string or bilingual langMap).

evidenceItem.description: Verifiable claim with source. Anti-pattern: unverifiable claims (dropped by cite-aware systems, §8).

credentialId.description: v1.4 (D17/§18.2): references `credentials[].id` — this claim is attested by that credential. Target resolved by core (load fails on a dangling ref).

artifactId.description: v1.4 (D17/§18.2): references `artifacts[].id` — this claim is proven by that artifact. Target resolved by core (load fails on a dangling ref).

authors.description: v1.1: author string (e.g. 'Luciani, C.' or 'Zambrano et al.').

url.description: v1.1: resolvable URL for outputs without DOI (preprint, conference abstract).

artifactRefs.description: v1.4 (D17/§18.1): references `artifacts[].id` — the dataset/code behind this paper. publications keep their domain (no duplication); targets resolved by core (load fails on a dangling ref).

publication.description: DOI/ORCID must be resolvable — GEO citability anchor (LLMs resolve them).

seo.description: Per-platform SEO keyword sets (fed by each platform skill's research).

platform.description: Dedup contract: MUST equal ['all', ...$defs/platform.enum] — scripts/schema-check asserts it (D16).

rule.description: Rule catalog (extensible). Skills' checks.yaml use the same catalog; `pasco check` runs the union. v1.1 (brand §17): handle-claimed (a claimed handle must resolve to a URL) and handle-consistent (handle matrix coherent across surfaces).

surface.description: Additive (#240): which text rows a char-limit rule applies to. Absent = both. A title cap can target `headline` without flagging the bio.

activeEntry.description: The chosen variant id — user picked it (D11); variant body lives in the workspace variants store.

entryId.description: v1.3 (D18, §19.2): stable entry id — the ledger address. Unique per block (core-checked, fails validation; JSON Schema cannot express uniqueness). Optional: rows without id are listed by `pasco status` as untracked.

origin.description: v1.3 (D18, §19.2): provenance — `template` marks the fictional examples shipped by profile-data-template. Absent = user-authored.

certification.description: v1.10 (issue #132, §19.5): the certification dimension over the live artifact — how the deploy was confirmed, and whether the live surface still matches. ORTHOGONAL to staleness: `stale` + `verified` is legal and meaningful. Optional (additive, semver minor): absent reads as `attested`, which is exactly what every record written before v1.10 was. The shape is not uniform — `state` selects the required fields (§19.5 fixes the shape; the verdict table and the rollup fix the semantics).

deploymentRecord.description: v1.3 (D18, §19.1): one confirmed deploy of a trackable unit on one surface. contentHash = SHA-256 of the canonical serialization (sorted keys, sans id/origin) of the unit AT deploy time — staleness is exact and release-tag-independent. v1.10 (issue #132, §19.5): the optional `certification` block adds the second, orthogonal dimension.

oneOf.description: §19.5 C1: a deterministic pass fetched the live artifact, applied the surface's extractor, and the live digest EQUALS the stored anchor. The fetch evidence is required — a `verified` with no fetch behind it is not evidence.

§19.5 C2: the human `--mark`. Certified by ASSERTION, never rendered as a bare `in-sync`. `artifactHash` is the anchor written at confirmation when the surface has an extractor; a mark on a surface without one records no anchor (the declared forward-only v1 limit, §19.5).

reason.description: §19.5: the declared reasons, the attempt reasons, and `http-<code>` for the ACTUAL status the pass observed. `http-` accepts ANY 3-digit code — an enum of just http-403/http-429 made a routine 404/500 write a ledger the next `load()` rejects (review F1). One alternation rather than `enum ∪ pattern`: the Zod generator cannot express that union (it degrades to an untyped schema, which its safety net refuses), so the alternatives are pinned by the pattern and by fixtures instead.

oneOf.description: §19.5: no deterministic check is possible, or one was attempted and did not complete. DECLARED reasons (walled · walled-con-api · no-extractor · no-artifact-url) are the PASS's knowledge — it states them for its own output and writes nothing, so a workspace needs no ledger row per walled platform and the file keeps only durable evidence; ATTEMPTED ones (http-<code> · network-error · unattributed · host-not-allowed) are RECORDED with the fetch evidence. `liveHash` is impossible here — a comparison would make the state lie; `artifactHash` is allowed because it is the deploy ANCHOR, not a comparison, and a failed check must not destroy it (§19.5: the anchor is left unchanged).

§19.5: a C1 check COMPLETED and contradicts the ledger — the live digest differs from the anchor. Positive contrary evidence, never a strength of confirmation: the report must not fold it into a green state. Both digests and the fetch evidence are required so the contradiction is auditable.

deploymentSurfaces.description: v1.3 (D18): surface → deploy record. Surface keys are the ONE platform enum (D16) — also core-checked post-Zod (gen-zod drops propertyNames).

brandVoice.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): tone matrix seed — overall tone (langMap), core values, words/tones to avoid. Per-platform voice refinement lives in the platform skill (§17).

url.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): direct profile URL. A claimed handle should carry one, or match an identity.links entry (drift rule handle-claimed-not-linked).

socialHandle.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): one row of the brand handle matrix (platform → handle + claim status). Seed source: the operator's brand-handles availability sweep (§17).

newsletterPlatform.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): newsletter hosts the engine models (Substack now, Ghost later).

newsletter.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): the brand's newsletter surface. The name/description double as the GEO-visible text (RSS/LLM-readable).

podcastPlatform.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): podcast distribution modeled in v1.1 (Spotify for Creators / standalone RSS).

podcast.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): the brand's podcast — show metadata + RSS (GEO-citable via RSS).

artifactRefs.description: v1.4 (D17/§18.1): references `artifacts[].id` — the work behind this mention. press keeps its domain (no duplication); targets resolved by core (load fails on a dangling ref).

pressItem.description: v1.1 (additive, brand): a media mention — outlet, headline, resolvable URL, date (verifiable claims, §8).

visibility.description: D17/§18.5: first-class visibility. Renderers emit only `public`; `unlisted` is shared on request (client DMs); `private` never leaves the workspace. Absent = public (the pre-registry profile was public by design — absence must not hide silently).

id.description: Registry id — referenced by evidence items (`credentialId`) and renderers. Unique per block (core re-checks post-Zod: load fails on duplicates; JSON Schema cannot express uniqueness).

credentialId.description: Issuer-side identifier (e.g. certificate serial). Certificates carry PII — visibility governs exposure (§18.5).

verifyUrl.description: THE verification pointer (§18.4: SSOT member — feeds badges and structured data verbatim).

expires.description: Optional → `credential-expiry` check warns when in the past (§18.8).

credential.description: v1.4 (D17, §18.2): a third-party attestation. JSON-LD payoff (§18.9): `Person.hasCredential` → `EducationalOccupationalCredential` (public only).

id.description: Registry id — referenced by evidence items (`artifactId`) and publications/press (`artifactRefs`). Unique per block (core re-checks post-Zod).

url.description: Remote pointer — emitted in renders (URL SSOT, §18.4) and live-link checked.

path.description: In-workspace `media/…` or external under PASCO_EVIDENCE_ROOT — capability matrix (§18.3): NEVER emitted as a public URL while the workspace is private (D14); reaches public surfaces only via renderer assets/ output (M8).

locator.description: Exactly one of `url` | `path` (§18.3 capability matrix). The oneOf expresses the XOR for JSON Schema consumers; the generated Zod cannot express required-without-property, so core re-checks the XOR post-Zod (D12 fail class, ledger precedent).

checksum.description: Immutable artifacts only (§18.6): recorded at compile for byte-stable bundling (M8).

license.description: Usage rights for the work (e.g. CC-BY-4.0).

tags.description: Multi-area selection (§18.9): renderers select by platform + lang + tags; one workspace, many areas.

artifact.description: v1.4 (D17, §18.2): a work or media item. JSON-LD payoff (§18.9): surfaces as CreativeWork/ImageGallery/VideoObject/Dataset per platform (renderer-curated, D5).

definition.description: v1.10 (issue #288): the canonical definition per language — one sentence of the form 'X is a …' an answer engine can quote verbatim. ≤ 160 chars per value (what an answer engine quotes); MUST contain the entity name — JSON Schema cannot express it: the check is `geo/canonical-definition` in geoCheck v2 (#289). EN required (langMap rule, D8/§11); the propertyNames restriction shares the langMap precedent (issue #86, F3 — gen-zod reconstructs it).

id.description: §19.2 id rules (issue #288) — the stable slug the block is reviewed by; not a ledger key (faq is root, not row-tracked).

q.description: v1.10 (#288): the question, ≤ 90 chars per value. Unique per workspace — JSON Schema cannot express it: it is a geoCheck v2 rule (#289, `geo/faq-coverage`); duplicates collapse into one answer surface.

a.description: v1.10 (#288): the answer, ≤ 320 chars per value — beyond that it is prose, not an answer. The owner's assertion (D11/D14), never invented copy.

source.description: v1.10 (#288): optional http(s) pointer backing the answer (the §5 scheme boundary) — an answer with no pointer is a claim (§8).

faqEntry.description: v1.10 (issue #288): ONE citable Q&A pair — the fact pair the `FAQPage` JSON-LD node projects (`structuredData()`); the answer is the owner's assertion, rendered deterministically (same curation rule as `bios[]`).
